chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Sadaqa, from a man from the people of Hulwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'It is more beloved to me that I walk to fulfill the need of a Muslim brother of mine than to free a thousand persons and to carry in the way of Allah upon a thousand saddled and harnessed horses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of fulfilling the needs of a Muslim brother according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the act of fulfilling a believer's specific need above major acts of worship like freeing slaves or jihad, underscoring the Shia emphasis on social solidarity (mu'akhat). This comparison highlights that practical assistance to the community is not merely a social duty but a profound spiritual merit that rivals or exceeds individual acts of devotion, reflecting the interconnectedness of faith and social responsibility in Twelver Shi'ism.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Haroun Bin Kharjat, from Sadaqa, from a man from the people of Hulwan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘If I<sup>asws</sup> were to walk regarding a Muslim brother of mine<sup>asws</sup>, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to free the necks of a thousand persons, and load a thousand horses in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, saddled and harnessed’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Harun ibn Kharijah from Sadaqah from a man of the people of Hulwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Walking to help my Muslim brother (in belief) is more beloved to me than setting free one thousand souls and donating one thousand horses, saddled and harnessed, ready for use in the way of Allah.”
